description: BatchNorm forward training (spatial mode, saved mean/inv-variance and running statistics) in the HIP_MLOPS_ENGINE region: rank 4 or 5, NCHW/NCDHW or NHWC/NDHWC strides, float/half/bfloat16 x and y with float scale, bias and statistics, N*H*W > 1, hw and n swept around the kernel-variant thresholds (hw 512/1024/4096, n 3/32/64/256/768) and powers of two +-1. Template: quick Batchnorm/Default (the fwd-train topology with every optional tensor: saved mean and inv-variance plus prev/next running mean and variance and a momentum; Variant2 drops the running statistics and the momentum, which also makes the GPU reference decline it). Epsilon and momentum are literals of the template and are not swept. The axis domain (default/narrow/wide/positive/constant/nonzero/zeros/large/subnormal/nan/inf) renders the fill of x (uid 5) in metadata.inputs; default is the quick sweep's -1..1; large keeps scale 32 (x magnitudes 16..32 stay far inside half range after normalization). For nan and inf, x stays free(-1,1) because one non-finite x element makes its whole channel's mean, variance and y non-finite; the special fill (5% of elements, at least one) goes on scale (uid 11) and prev_running_mean/variance (uids 9, 10), which are per-channel and local: a poisoned scale makes only that channel's y non-finite and a poisoned prev running stat only its next-running element, while mean/inv_variance and the other channels stay finite. bias is not poisoned (with scale it could cover every channel of a small c); c == 1 makes every channel non-finite, which fails under match_nonfinite by design. The validator is match_nonfinite exactly for nan and inf. The other inputs keep their tuned literal ranges. The last axes, alignment (1..256) and placement (default/exact/under), declare that alignment on every device tensor (tensor_patches on uids 0-6 and 9-11; epsilon and momentum, uids 7 and 8, are pass-by-value scalars and are not patched) and place the run's pointers accordingly; under misaligns x (placement_uid 5) and needs alignment >= 2, so eff_placement turns under into exact at alignment 1.

derive.d: ds if ndim == 5 and (hw // h) % ds == 0 else 1
derive.dims_x: [n, c, h, w] if ndim == 4 else [n, c, d, h, w]
derive.xs_h: w if layout == 'nchw' else w * c
derive.xs_d: h * w if layout == 'nchw' else h * w * c
derive.xs_c: d * h * w if layout == 'nchw' else 1
derive.stride_x: [xs_n, xs_c, xs_h, xs_w] if ndim == 4 else [xs_n, xs_c, xs_d, xs_h, xs_w]
derive.stride_s: [c, 1, ss_w, ss_w] if ndim == 4 else [c, 1, ss_w, ss_w, ss_w]
derive.dom_kind: 'fixed' if domain == 'constant' else 'nonzero' if domain == 'nonzero' else 'zeros' if domain == 'zeros' else 'large' if domain == 'large' else 'subnormal' if domain == 'subnormal' else 'free'
derive.dom_lo: -0.01 if domain == 'narrow' else -8.0 if domain == 'wide' else 0.25 if domain == 'positive' else 0.5 if domain == 'constant' else -1.0
derive.dom_hi: 0.01 if domain == 'narrow' else 8.0 if domain == 'wide' else 4.0 if domain == 'positive' else 0.5 if domain == 'constant' else 1.0
derive.eff_placement: 'exact' if placement == 'under' and alignment < 2 else placement

constraints.reason: training computes batch statistics, so N * spatial must be > 1 (frontend validateBatchNormTrainingSpatialDimensions, Utilities.hpp:140; engine BatchnormValidator::validateSpatialDimensions, BatchnormApplicabilityChecks.cpp:29)

GPU reference cost ceiling for normalization ops (RFC 0023 section 14); also keeps HIP_PLUGIN_BN_NCHW/NHW/CHW inside the int template parameters of the kernel (Configuration.hpp proto_config, BatchnormFwdTrainingPlan.cpp:393-396)
